## Body

#307 (F250) at c8d457f: pass-with-notes, output 9dc94af2.

How to judge a local trust record: ask what it can upgrade, not only whether it can be forged. Same-user forgery is always cheap under C33. Here verdict() runs only after the contract executes every check in the same invocation, and a failure returns before any record is read. Every full pass on the installed SDK writes its own record first. So a forged record can only turn warn into pass on an --sdk or --copilot-version run whose own checks passed. update-copilot uses neither flag. Prove it with probes, not reading: forged record plus a broken --sdk module gave fail, and forged record plus the real --sdk gave pass. Run them in a scratch PIJ_RS_STATE_DIR.

Probe kit that worked (node directly on the .mjs; the review worktree has no node_modules, so no vitest):
- path-shaped versions: ../x, a/b, .hidden, .., a trailing \n, the empty string, 65 chars;
- a symlinked record, where the write must rename over the link and leave its target untouched;
- a FIFO record (O_NONBLOCK plus isFile);
- a case alias, which matters on APFS: the in-record version check must catch it.

Watch for parity claims with Rust paths. S307-N1: the JS no-HOME fallback (tmpdir/pij-rs-no-home) lacks the /.pij-rs that Rust default_state_dir uses, and on Linux that lands in the shared /tmp.

Trap: Copilot updated itself mid-review (-3 to -4). Read the version at probe time, and parse it exactly: my grep grabbed a trailing dot.
